must_remember: The orbital angular momentum of an electron in the n-th Bohr orbit is quantized as $L = nh / (2\pi)$.
The radius of the n-th Bohr orbit varies as $r_n \propto n^2 / Z$ with the ground state value of $0.529 \text{ \AA}$ for hydrogen.
The orbital velocity of an electron in the n-th orbit varies inversely with the principal quantum number $n$ ($v_n \propto Z / n$).
The total energy of an electron in a Bohr orbit is negative, indicating a bound state, and is given by $E_n = -13.6 Z^2 / n^2 \text{ eV}$.
Transitions terminating at $n = 1$ give the Lyman series (ultraviolet), while $n = 2$ gives the Balmer series (visible).
Finite nuclear mass correction replaces the electron mass $m$ with the reduced mass $\mu = (m \cdot M) / (m + M)$.

glossary.meaning: Permitted orbits in which an electron does not radiate electromagnetic energy despite continuous acceleration.
Effective mass used to correct for finite nuclear mass when the nucleus is not infinitely heavy compared to the orbiting electron.
A fundamental physical constant governing the wave numbers of emitted or absorbed spectral lines in hydrogen-like atoms.
The energy required to completely remove an electron from the ground state ($n = 1$) to infinity ($n = \infty$).
